thought.text: Keycloak is up with the realm imported. Now let me verify the JWKS, token endpoint, and logins:

reasoning_content:
**Keycloak is now running with the startuphafen realm imported!**

Next steps:
1. Verify that the realm's clients, users, and JWKS are reachable.
2. Test login with alice/alice via the token endpoint.
3. Start the backend (node dist) and verify the DB migration + the /trpc health check.
4. Verify the frontend is being served and that caddy proxies everything.

Let me test the token endpoint directly:
curl -X POST http://localhost:28080/realms/startuphafen/protocol/openid-connect/token -d "client_id=startuphafen_app&grant_type=password&username=alice&password=alice"

tool_call.name: terminal
tool_call.arguments: {"command": "curl -s http://localhost:28080/realms/startuphafen/protocol/openid-connect/certs | head -c 300; echo; echo \"=== login alice ===\"\ncurl -s -o /tmp/token.json -w \"%{http_code}\\n\" -X POST http://localhost:28080/realms/startuphafen/protocol/openid-connect/token -d \"client_id=startuphafen_app&grant_type=password&username=alice&password=alice\"\nnode -e \"const t=require('/tmp/token.json'); console.log('token type:', t.token_type, '| error:', t.error); const jwt=t.access_token||''; const p=jwt.split('.'); if(p[1]){const b64=p[1].replace(/-/g,'+').replace(/_/g,'/'); console.log('claims:', JSON.stringify(JSON.parse(Buffer.from(b64+ '=='.slice(0,(4-b64.length%4)%4),'base64').toString())));}\" 2>&1 | head -5", "description": "Verify JWKS and alice token login", "security_risk": "UNKNOWN", "summary": "Verify JWKS and alice login"}
